issues.legal_issue: The claimants did not establish that the disputed properties remained joint-family properties available for partition.
material_facts: The claimants sought partition of properties said to have belonged to the ancestral family or to have been acquired by it.
Documents showed separate money-lending and other dealings by individual family members, and separate tax assessments of their properties.
A claimant had stated in a separate proceeding that the families had not been joint since an earlier period; the statement was not explained, and the partition suit was brought decades later.
The documents relied on to support continued jointness, including correspondence and an account sheet, did not establish that the business or properties belonged to a joint family.
The High Court dismissed the partition suit, and the Supreme Court considered the documentary evidence on appeal.
issues.conclusion: The claimants failed to establish a right to partition; the High Court’s dismissal of the suit was affirmed and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court recognized that a member of an undivided Hindu joint family may carry on a separate business, so separate dealings do not by themselves establish that the family has separated. The evidence must be assessed as a whole. Here, the admission of separation, the documentary evidence of individual dealings and separate assessments, and the inadequacy of the evidence offered to show continued jointness supported the finding that the parties were separate and that the properties were not established as joint-family property. The judgment relied on no statutory provision or earlier case.

rule.if: partition_suit_appeal and separation_admission and delayed_partition_claim and individual_property_dealings and separate_property_assessments and joint_family_evidence_inadequate

predicates.partition_suit_appeal: Claimants brought a suit seeking partition and appealed after the suit was dismissed by the appellate court.
predicates.separation_admission: A claimant stated in a separate proceeding that the families had ceased to be joint.
predicates.delayed_partition_claim: The claimants sought partition decades after the stated separation, without pleading that separation as the basis of their claim.
predicates.individual_property_dealings: Documents showed family members carrying out money-lending or other dealings individually.
predicates.separate_property_assessments: Records showed property assessed separately in individual family members’ names.
predicates.joint_family_evidence_inadequate: The documents offered to support continued joint ownership did not establish that the disputed business or properties belonged to the joint family.

issues.definition: When claimants seek partition but the evidence includes an admission of separation, a long delay before claiming partition, individual dealings, separate property assessments, and inadequate evidence of continued joint ownership, the partition claim is not established.
